content: 1. For individuals seeking information about abortion care, either before treatment or following an incomplete abortion or complications (medical or surgical, at any gestational age), the provision of information and referral to abortion services by pharmacy workers is evaluated as a satisfactory and acceptable alternative to the usual practice of providing no information. The outcomes assessed include the effectiveness of pharmacy workers' knowledge of safe abortion practices, post-abortion care, and indications for referral, as well as the privacy, accessibility, and satisfaction with the information and services provided. 2. For pregnant individuals undergoing an abortion, preand post-abortion counseling provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, pharmacists, pharmacy workers, or community health workers is assessed as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to counseling provided by in-clinic staff such as generalist or specialist medical practitioners, nurses, or midwives. Outcomes include the effectiveness of counseling in terms of knowledge of contraceptive options, safe abortion services, and post-abortion care, as well as satisfaction, accessibility, privacy, and quality of counseling. 3. For pregnant individuals undergoing a surgical abortion, the use of cervical priming with osmotic dilators or medications provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, associate/advanced associate clinicians, midwives, nurses, or auxiliary nurse midwives is evaluated as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to cervical priming performed by physicians. Outcomes include safety (serious adverse events and complications), effectiveness (degree of cervical dilation and ease of procedure), and satisfaction. 4. For pregnant individuals seeking an induced abortion or treatment for incomplete abortion or miscarriage, vacuum aspiration provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, auxiliary nurse midwives, or auxiliary nurses is assessed as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to vacuum aspiration performed by generalist or specialist medical practitioners. Outcomes include safety (serious adverse events and complications), effectiveness (success of abortion following the procedure), and satisfaction. 5. For pregnant individuals seeking surgical abortion at ≥14 weeks of gestation, dilation and evacuation (D&E) provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, associate/advanced associate clinicians, or midwives is evaluated as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to care provided by generalist and specialist medical practitioners. Outcomes include effectiveness (success of abortion following the procedure), safety (serious adverse events and complications), and satisfaction. 6. For pregnant individuals diagnosed with intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD), medical management with mifepristone and misoprostol, or misoprostol alone, provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, associate/advanced associate clinicians, midwives, nurses, auxiliary nurses, pharmacists, pharmacy workers, or community health workers is assessed as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to management by physicians. Outcomes include safety (serious adverse events and complications), effectiveness (success of abortion without surgical intervention), and satisfaction. 7. For pregnant individuals with incomplete abortion at gestational ages <14 weeks, management with misoprostol provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, pharmacists, pharmacy workers, or community health workers is evaluated as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to management with misoprostol provided by physicians. Outcomes include safety (serious adverse events and complications), effectiveness (success of abortion without surgical intervention), and satisfaction. 8. For pregnant individuals seeking induced abortion, vacuum aspiration for uncomplicated incomplete abortion provided by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, auxiliary nurses, or auxiliary nurse midwives is assessed as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to vacuum aspiration performed by physicians. Outcomes include safety (serious adverse events and complications), effectiveness (success of abortion following the procedure), and satisfaction. 9. For individuals presenting with complications of an induced abortion in a stable condition, diagnosis and management of abortion-related complications (e.g., infection or hemorrhage) by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, pharmacists, pharmacy workers, or community health workers is evaluated as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to diagnosis and management by physicians. Outcomes include effectiveness (accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment or referral), safety (serious adverse events), and satisfaction. 10. For individuals in the post-abortion period requiring contraception, the provision of injectable contraceptives (initiation or continuation) by traditional and complementary medicine professionals, pharmacists, pharmacy workers, or community health workers is assessed as a safe, effective, and satisfactory alternative to provision by generalist or specialist medical practitioners. Outcomes include safety, effectiveness, and satisfaction.
